sanskrit: śukraṁ te anyad yajataṁ te anyad viṣurūpe ahanī dyaur ivāsi | viśvā hi māyā avasi svadhāvo bhadrā te pūṣann iha rātir astu ||
english: One of your forms is radiant, another is adorable; you are like the sky, O you of two-fold aspect, of twin days. For you, O self-sustaining one, do ward off all illusions; may your gift here be auspicious, O Pūṣan.

sanskrit: ajāśvaḥ paśupā vājapastyo dhiyaṁjinvo bhuvane viśve arpitaḥ | aṣṭrām pūṣā śithirām udvarīvṛjat saṁcakṣāṇo bhuvanā deva īyate ||
english: Goat-horsed, herdsman, dwelling on viands, stimulated by prayers, set in all the worlds — Pūṣan, brandishing his loose goad overhead, the god moves on surveying all the realms.

sanskrit: yās te pūṣan nāvo antaḥ samudre hiraṇyayīr antarikṣe caranti | tābhir yāsi dūtyāṁ sūryasya kāmena kṛta śrava icchamānaḥ ||
english: Those golden ships of yours, O Pūṣan, that move within the ocean, within the mid-air — with them you travel on the errand of Sūrya, you who are made by desire, seeking renown.

sanskrit: pūṣā subandhur diva ā pṛthivyā iḻas patir maghavā dasmavarcāḥ | yaṁ devāso adaduḥ sūryāyai kāmena kṛtaṁ tavasaṁ svañcam ||
english: Pūṣan, good kinsman of heaven and earth, lord of refreshment, bounteous, of wondrous lustre — he whom the gods gave to Sūryā, made by desire, mighty and fair of form.

sanskrit: pra nu vocā suteṣu vāṁ vīryā3 yāni cakrathuḥ | hatāso vām pitaro devaśatrava indrāgnī jīvatho yuvam ||
english: Now at the soma pressings let me proclaim the heroic deeds that you two have accomplished. The fathers who were foes of the gods have been slain by you — O Indra and Agni, you two live on.

sanskrit: baḻ itthā mahimā vām indrāgnī paniṣṭha ā | samāno vāṁ janitā bhrātarā yuvaṁ yamāv ihehamātarā ||
english: Verily thus, O Indra and Agni, your greatness is most worthy of praise from every side. You have one birthplace; you two are brothers — you are like twins, sharing a common mother here and there.

sanskrit: okivāṁsā sute sacām̐ aśvā saptī ivādane | indrā nv a1gnī avaseha vajriṇā vayaṁ devā havāmahe ||
english: Dwelling together when the soma is pressed, like two horses at the trough — we here invoke Indra and Agni, the two gods, the thunderbolt-bearing ones, for protection.

sanskrit: ya indrāgnī suteṣu vāṁ stavat teṣv ṛtāvṛdhā | joṣavākaṁ vadataḥ pajrahoṣiṇā na devā bhasathaś cana ||
english: He who praises you two, O Indra and Agni, O increasers of cosmic order, at the soma pressings — to him you two speak words of approval, you who roar like Pajra's flame; as gods you never fail him.

sanskrit: indrāgnī ko asya vāṁ devau martaś ciketati | viṣūco aśvān yuyujāna īyata ekaḥ samāna ā rathe ||
english: O Indra and Agni, what mortal truly comprehends this greatness of yours? He who yokes horses turned in different directions goes on, alone, yet on the same chariot.

sanskrit: indrāgnī apād iyam pūrvāgāt padvatībhyaḥ | hitvī śiro jihvayā vāvadac carat triṁśat padā ny akramīt ||
english: O Indra and Agni, this one footless has gone forth before the footed. Having abandoned its head, it speaks with its tongue and goes; it has trodden down thirty footsteps.

sanskrit: indrāgnī ā hi tanvate naro dhanvāni bāhvoḥ | mā no asmin mahādhane parā varktaṁ gaviṣṭiṣu ||
english: O Indra and Agni, men stretch their bows upon their arms; do not cut us off from this great prize in the battles for cattle.

sanskrit: indrāgnī tapanti māghā aryo arātayaḥ | apa dveṣāṁsy ā kṛtaṁ yuyutaṁ sūryād adhi ||
english: O Indra and Agni, the grudging foes of the noble man scorch away his wealth; ward off all enmities, keep them separate, above the sun.

sanskrit: indrāgnī yuvor api vasu divyāni pārthivā | ā na iha pra yacchataṁ rayiṁ viśvāyupoṣasam ||
english: O Indra and Agni, the celestial and earthly treasures belong to you both; bestow on us here the riches that nourish all life.

sanskrit: indrāgnī ukthavāhasā stomebhir havanaśrutā | viśvābhir gīrbhir ā gatam asya somasya pītaye ||
english: O Indra and Agni, bearers of lauds, who hear the invocation in the praises, come hither with all our hymns for the drinking of this soma.

sanskrit: śnathad vṛtram uta sanoti vājam indrā yo agnī sahurī saparyāt | irajyantā vasavyasya bhūreḥ sahastamā sahasā vājayantā ||
english: He who would worship Indra and Agni, the pair mighty in strength, shall smite Vṛtra and win the prize; swaying together, sharing great wealth, most hand-clasped, overcoming with their power.

sanskrit: tā yodhiṣṭam abhi gā indra nūnam apaḥ svar uṣaso agna ūḻhāḥ | diśaḥ svar uṣasa indra citrā apo gā agne yuvase niyutvān ||
english: O Indra, fight now for the cows; O Agni, the waters, the sunlight, the dawns have been carried off! The directions, the brilliant sunlight, the dawns — O Indra; the waters, the cows — O Agni, you unite them with your teams.

sanskrit: ā vṛtrahaṇā vṛtrahabhiḥ śuṣmair indra yātaṁ namobhir agne arvāk | yuvaṁ rādhobhir akavebhir indrāgne asme bhavatam uttamebhiḥ ||
english: O Vṛtra-slayers, come hither with your Vṛtra-slaying powers, O Indra; with obeisances, O Agni — come forward. O Indra and Agni, be present among us with your supreme and unerring bounties.

sanskrit: tā huve yayor idam papne viśvam purā kṛtam | indrāgnī na mardhataḥ ||
english: I invoke these two by whom all this universe was acquired and made long ago — Indra and Agni, who neglect no one.

sanskrit: ugrā vighaninā mṛdha indrāgnī havāmahe | tā no mṛḻāta īdṛśe ||
english: We invoke Indra and Agni, the fierce crushers of battles; may those two be gracious to us in such a case.

sanskrit: hato vṛtrāṇy āryā hato dāsāni satpatī | hato viśvā apa dviṣaḥ ||
english: Slay the Vṛtras befitting the noble man, O true lords; slay the Dāsa ones; slay and drive away all adversaries.

sanskrit: indrāgnī yuvām ime3 'bhi stomā anūṣata | pibataṁ śambhuvā sutam ||
english: O Indra and Agni, these lauds have sung out toward you both; drink the pressed soma, you who bring welfare.

sanskrit: yā vāṁ santi puruspṛho niyuto dāśuṣe narā | indrāgnī tābhir ā gatam ||
english: O Indra and Agni, those many-desired teams that belong to you, O heroes, for the worshipper — come hither with those.

sanskrit: tābhir ā gacchataṁ naropedaṁ savanaṁ sutam | indrāgnī somapītaye ||
english: Come hither with those teams, O Indra and Agni, to this pressing of the soma for the drinking of it.

sanskrit: tam īḻiṣva yo arciṣā vanā viśvā pariṣvajat | kṛṣṇā kṛṇoti jihvayā ||
english: Worship that one who embraces all forests with his flame, who makes them black with his tongue.

sanskrit: ya iddha āvivāsati sumnam indrasya martyaḥ | dyumnāya sutarā apaḥ ||
english: That mortal who, when kindled, seeks the favour of Indra — for him are the waters most easily crossed for the sake of glory.

sanskrit: tā no vājavatīr iṣa āśūn pipṛtam arvataḥ | indram agniṁ ca voḻhave ||
english: Fill us with refreshment rich in prizes; fill our swift steeds — to carry Indra and Agni.

sanskrit: ubhā vām indrāgnī āhuvadhyā ubhā rādhasaḥ saha mādayadhyai | ubhā dātārāv iṣāṁ rayīṇām ubhā vājasya sātaye huve vām ||
english: O Indra and Agni, you two are both to be invoked; both are to be gladdened together with bounty; both are givers of refreshment and riches; I invoke you both for the winning of the prize.

sanskrit: ā no gavyebhir aśvyair vasavyai3r upa gacchatam | sakhāyau devau sakhyāya śambhuvendrāgnī tā havāmahe ||
english: Come to us with prizes of cattle and horses and wealth; we invoke you two, Indra and Agni, friends among the gods, for friendship, for welfare.

sanskrit: indrāgnī śṛṇutaṁ havaṁ yajamānasya sunvataḥ | vītaṁ havyāny ā gatam pibataṁ somyam madhu ||
english: O Indra and Agni, hear the invocation of the sacrificer who presses soma; enjoy the oblations, come hither, drink the sweet soma-draught.

sanskrit: iyam adadād rabhasam ṛṇacyutaḥ divodāsaṁ vadhryaśvāya dāśuṣe | yā śaśvantam ācakhādāvasam paṇiṁ tā te dātrāṇi taviṣā sarasvati ||
english: She — who has shaken off debt — gave the impetuous Divodāsa to Vadhryaśva who was a worshipper; she who for ever has gnawed down the settled Paṇi — these are your mighty gifts, O Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: iyaṁ śuṣmebhir bisakhā ivārujat sānu girīṇāṁ taviṣebhir ūrmibhiḥ | pārāvataghnīm avase suvṛktibhiḥ sarasvatīm ā vivāsema dhītibhiḥ ||
english: With her impetus she broke open the ridges of the mountains like a stalk of lotus, with her mighty waves; with purifying prayers and right praises may we seek after Sarasvatī, destroyer of the far-away (foe), for protection.

sanskrit: sarasvati devanido ni barhaya prajāṁ viśvasya bṛsayasya māyinaḥ | uta kṣitibhyo 'vanīr avindo viṣam ebhyo asravo vājinīvati ||
english: O Sarasvatī, crush down the offspring of every deceitful reviler of the gods; and you, O prize-mistress, have found streams from the waters for the settlements — poison has flowed away from them.

sanskrit: pra ṇo devī sarasvatī vājebhir vājinīvatī | dhīnām avitry avatu ||
english: May divine Sarasvatī, rich in prizes, bounteous with prizes, protect us as the nurturer of thoughts.

sanskrit: yas tvā devi sarasvaty upabrūte dhane hite | indraṁ na vṛtratūrye ||
english: He who, O goddess Sarasvatī, addresses you when treasure is set as the stake — as Indra in the conquest of Vṛtra.

sanskrit: tvaṁ devi sarasvaty avā vājeṣu vājini | radā pūṣeva naḥ sanim ||
english: You, O prize-rich goddess Sarasvatī, afford us protection in the contests; grant us acquisition like Pūṣan.

sanskrit: uta syā naḥ sarasvatī ghorā hiraṇyavartaniḥ | vṛtraghnī vaṣṭi suṣṭutim ||
english: And indeed this Sarasvatī of ours, dread one, whose path is of gold, the Vṛtra-slayer, desires well-uttered praise.

sanskrit: yasyā ananto ahrutas tveṣaś cariṣṇur arṇavaḥ | amaś carati roruvat ||
english: She whose impetuous, unstoppable, agitated flood moves on; whose might goes forward roaring.

sanskrit: sā no viśvā ati dviṣaḥ svasṝr anyā ṛtāvarī | atann aheva sūryaḥ ||
english: May she — surpassing all adversaries, superior to other sisters, maintaining cosmic order — extend over us like the sun of the day.

sanskrit: uta naḥ priyā priyāsu saptasvasā sujuṣṭā | sarasvatī stomyā bhūt ||
english: And may Sarasvatī, beloved among the beloved, seven-sistered, pleasing, be worthy of our praise.

sanskrit: āpapruṣī pārthivāny uru rajo antarikṣam | sarasvatī nidas pātu ||
english: Filling the earthly realms, the wide space, the mid-air — may Sarasvatī protect us from reproaches.

sanskrit: triṣadhasthā saptadhātuḥ pañca jātā vardhayantī | vāje-vāje havyā bhūt ||
english: Throned in the three places, sevenfold in substance, born of five, the one who increases — may she be invoked at every contest.

sanskrit: pra yā mahimnā mahināsu cekite dyumnebhir anyā apasām apastamā | ratha iva bṛhatī vibhvane kṛtopastutyā cikituṣā sarasvatī ||
english: She who among the great ones shines forth with greatness in her glories, most active of the active, far surpassing others — Sarasvatī, great like a chariot set in motion for the all-pervading, worthy of secondary praise, perceptive.

sanskrit: sarasvaty abhi no neṣi vasyo māpa spharīḥ payasā mā na ā dhak | juṣasva naḥ sakhyā veśyā ca mā tvat kṣetrāṇy araṇāni ganma ||
english: O Sarasvatī, lead us forward to better fortune; do not deprive us of your milk, do not scorch us; accept our friendship and our offerings; may we not go from you to alien fields.

sanskrit: stuṣe narā divo asya prasantāśvinā huve jaramāṇo arkaiḥ | yā sadya usrā vyuṣi jmo antān yuyūṣataḥ pary urū varāṁsi ||
english: I praise those heroic, renowned lords of this heaven; I invoke the Aśvinā as I grow old, with my hymns — who, going forth immediately at dawn's breaking, and desiring to reach the ends of the earth, drive around the wide realms.

sanskrit: tā yajñam ā śucibhiś cakramāṇā rathasya bhānuṁ rurucū rajobhiḥ | purū varāṁsy amitā mimānāpo dhanvāny ati yātho ajrān ||
english: Those two, advancing to the sacrifice with bright rites, have illumined the radiance of the chariot with their luminous regions; having measured out many immeasurable realms, you two journey beyond the waters, beyond the deserts, through the open plains.

sanskrit: tā ha tyad vartir yad aradhram ugretthā dhiya ūhathuḥ śaśvad aśvaiḥ | manojavebhir iṣiraiḥ śayadhyai pari vyathir dāśuṣo martyasya ||
english: Verily, you two drove that chariot — the one that is never idle — in just this mighty fashion, ever with your horses swift as thought, restless, to ward off the distress of the worshipping mortal.

sanskrit: tā navyaso jaramāṇasya manmopa bhūṣato yuyujānasaptī | śubham pṛkṣam iṣam ūrjaṁ vahantā hotā yakṣat pratno adhrug yuvānā ||
english: May the ancient Hotṛ who harms none sacrifice to those two ever-young ones who come, adorning themselves, toward the fresh praise of the aged one who sings, who have yoked their steeds, who carry nourishment, refreshment, and strength.

sanskrit: tā valgū dasrā puruśākatamā pratnā navyasā vacasā vivāse | yā śaṁsate stuvate śambhaviṣṭhā babhūvatur gṛṇate citrarātī ||
english: Those two fair ones, wondrous Dasras, most richly gleaming, ancient yet ever-new in speech, do I seek with my word — those who have become most beneficent to the celebrant and the praiser, of brilliant bounty to the singer.

sanskrit: tā bhujyuṁ vibhir adbhyaḥ samudrāt tugrasya sūnum ūhathū rajobhiḥ | areṇubhir yojanebhir bhujantā patatribhir arṇaso nir upasthāt ||
english: You two conveyed Bhujyu out of the ocean, out of the waters, the son of Tugra, through the luminous regions, enjoying it with dustless journeys, with winged ones, from the lap of the flood.

sanskrit: vi jayuṣā rathyā yātam adriṁ śrutaṁ havaṁ vṛṣaṇā vadhrimatyāḥ | daśasyantā śayave pipyathur gām iti cyavānā sumatim bhuraṇyū ||
english: O bulls, with your victorious, chariot-going power, cleave through the mountain; hear the invocation of Vadhrimatī; honouring her wish, you two swelled the cow for Śayave — thus moved, you two sustainers showed favour.

sanskrit: yad rodasī pradivo asti bhūmā heḻo devānām uta martyatrā | tad ādityā vasavo rudriyāso rakṣoyuje tapur aghaṁ dadhāta ||
english: Whatever sin there may be from long ago in the two worlds, whatever offence against the gods or among mortals — that, O Ādityas, Vasus, and Rudra groups, joined together for protection, lay as burning guilt.

sanskrit: ya īṁ rājānāv ṛtuthā vidadhad rajaso mitro varuṇaś ciketat | gambhīrāya rakṣase hetim asya droghāya cid vacasa ānavāya ||
english: He who appoints those two kings in due season — Mitra and Varuṇa take note of the region; for the deep demon of the dark they place his weapon — even for him who speaks deceitfully.

sanskrit: antaraiś cakrais tanayāya vartir dyumatā yātaṁ nṛvatā rathena | sanutyena tyajasā martyasya vanuṣyatām api śīrṣā vavṛktam ||
english: Come with wheels within wheels, with a brilliant, man-bearing chariot, for the sake of offspring; with the ancient abandonment of what is mortal, turn the heads of those who would injure.

sanskrit: ā paramābhir uta madhyamābhir niyudbhir yātam avamābhir arvāk | dṛḻhasya cid gomato vi vrajasya duro vartaṁ gṛṇate citrarātī ||
english: Come hither with the highest teams and also with the middlemost, with the lowest — come forward; open the doors even of the firm, cow-filled enclosure for the singer, O you of brilliant bounty.

sanskrit: kva1 tyā valgū puruhūtādya dūto na stomo 'vidan namasvān | ā yo arvāṅ nāsatyā vavarta preṣṭhā hy asatho asya manman ||
english: Where are those fair Nāsatyas, much invoked, today? The reverent praise, like a messenger, has not found them. He who has turned toward us the most beloved pair — for you are most dear to this thought of his.

sanskrit: aram me gantaṁ havanāyāsmai gṛṇānā yathā pibātho andhaḥ | pari ha tyad vartir yāthio riṣo na yat paro nāntaras tuturyāt ||
english: Come readily to his invocation, singing together, as you drink the soma juice; go driving around in that chariot against harms so that neither one far nor one near may outstrip.

sanskrit: akāri vām andhaso varīmann astāri barhiḥ suprāyaṇatamam | uttānahasto yuvayur vavandā vāṁ nakṣanto adraya ā ñjan ||
english: The soma has been prepared for you two in abundance; the most easily approached sacred grass has been strewn; with uplifted hand, youthful, I have praised you — the pressing stones anointed, coming toward you.

sanskrit: ūrdhvo vām agnir adhvareṣv asthāt pra rātir eti jūrṇinī ghṛtācī | pra hotā gūrtamanā urāṇo 'yukta yo nāsatyā havīman ||
english: The fire has stood upright for you two at the sacrifices; the gladdening gift, clarified and flame-lit, goes forward; the Hotṛ, delighted in mind, expansive, who is invoker for the Nāsatyas, has been set in motion.

sanskrit: adhi śriye duhitā sūryasya rathaṁ tasthau purubhujā śatotim | pra māyābhir māyinā bhūtam atra narā nṛtū janiman yajñiyānām ||
english: Sūrya's daughter has mounted the chariot for glory, the one that gives much and has a hundred aids; O men skilled at dancing, become here surpassers with your arts at the birth of the sacrifice-worthy ones.

sanskrit: yuvaṁ śrībhir darśatābhir ābhiḥ śubhe puṣṭim ūhathuḥ sūryāyāḥ | pra vāṁ vayo vapuṣe 'nu paptan nakṣad vāṇī suṣṭutā dhiṣṇyā vām ||
english: With these visible beauties you two have brought nourishment for the loveliness of Sūryā; your birds have flown forward for your beauty — the voice, when well praised, shall reach your divine seat.

sanskrit: ā vāṁ vayo 'śvāso vahiṣṭhā abhi prayo nāsatyā vahantu | pra vāṁ ratho manojavā asarjīṣaḥ pṛkṣa iṣidho anu pūrvīḥ ||
english: Let the swiftest horses, O Nāsatyas, carry your birds toward your refreshment; your chariot has been swift as thought, released, following the ancient streams of nourishment.

sanskrit: puru hi vām purubhujā deṣṇaṁ dhenuṁ na iṣam pinvatam asakrām | stutaś ca vām mādhvī suṣṭutiś ca rasāś ca ye vām anu rātim agman ||
english: O bounteous ones who enjoy much, you have given much to us; swell for us refreshment like a milk-cow flowing without cease; both the sweet praise and the well-uttered praise are lauded to you, and the essences that have reached after your bounty.

sanskrit: uta ma ṛjre purayasya raghvī sumīḻhe śatam peruke ca pakvā | śāṇḍo dād dhiraṇinaḥ smaddiṣṭīn daśa vaśāso abhiṣāca ṛṣvān ||
english: Also for me from the swift one of the city Ṛjra, well-rewarded, a hundred ripe ones of Peruku; Śāṇḍa has given golden, well-aimed gifts — ten choice cows, noble, and approaching ones.

sanskrit: saṁ vāṁ śatā nāsatyā sahasrāśvānām purupanthā gire dāt | bharadvājāya vīra nū gire dāt dhatā rakṣāṁsi purudaṁsasā syuḥ ||
english: Purupanthā has given for the hymn to you two Nāsatyas a hundred of the thousand-horsed; now, O hero, has given for the hymn to Bharadvāja; may you, of many wonders, lay the demons low.

sanskrit: ā vāṁ sumne variman sūribhiḥ ṣyām ||
english: May we be in your favour, in your breadth, O Aśvins, with the patrons.

sanskrit: ud u śriya uṣaso rocamānā asthur apāṁ normayo ruśantaḥ | kṛṇoti viśvā supathā sugāny abhūd u vasvī dakṣiṇā maghonī ||
english: The splendours of the glowing dawn have risen up like the shining waves of the waters; she makes all roads easy, all paths good; the bounteous sacrificial fee has become rich and reward-bestowing.

sanskrit: bhadrā dadṛkṣa urviyā vi bhāsy ut te śocir bhānavo dyām apaptan | āvir vakṣaḥ kṛṇuṣe śumbhamānoṣo devi rocamānā mahobhiḥ ||
english: Auspicious to behold, you shine forth widely; your flames and rays have leapt up to the sky; you reveal your breast, adorning yourself, O goddess Uṣas, shining with your might.

sanskrit: vahanti sīm aruṇāso ruśantao gāvaḥ subhagām urviyā prathānām | apejate śūro asteva śatrūn bādhate tamo ajiro na voḻhā ||
english: The red, shining cows carry her onward, the fortunate one spreading widely; the hero drives away the enemies like arrows; swift darkness presses back like a carrier.

sanskrit: sugota te supathā parvateṣv avāte apas tarasi svabhāno | sā na ā vaha pṛthuyāmann ṛṣve rayiṁ divo duhitar iṣayadhyai ||
english: Good are your paths, good your roads on the mountains, without wind you cross the waters, O self-luminous one; bring to us, O daughter of heaven, riches to enjoy as you travel broadly.

sanskrit: sā vaha yokṣabhir avātoṣo varaṁ vahasi joṣam anu | tvaṁ divo duhitar yā ha devī pūrvahūtau maṁhanā darśatā bhūḥ ||
english: So bring it, with your yoke-fellows, O Dawn moving without wind; you carry what is best in accordance with pleasure; you, goddess, daughter of heaven, who in the first invocation were resplendent and visible.

sanskrit: ut te vayaś cid vasater apaptan naraś ca ye pitubhājo vyuṣṭau | amā sate vahasi bhūri vāmam uṣo devi dāśuṣe martyāya ||
english: Even the birds have flown forth from their resting place, and men who share in food at your shining; you carry much that is lovely to one who stays at home, O goddess Uṣas, for the mortal worshipper.

sanskrit: eṣā syā no duhitā divojāḥ kṣitīr ucchantī mānuṣīr ajīgaḥ | yā bhānunā ruśatā rāmyāsv ajñāyi tiras tamasaś cid aktūn ||
english: This daughter of heaven, sprung from the sky, has stirred up the human settlements as she shines; who has been recognised by her gleaming radiance in the beautiful nights, piercing through the dark shadows.

sanskrit: vi tad yayur aruṇayugbhir aśvaiś citram bhānty uṣasaś candrarathāḥ ||aggraṁ yajñasya bṛhato nayantīr vi tā bādhante tama ūrmyāyāḥ ||
english: The moon-charioted dawns shine brilliantly with their red-yoked horses; those that lead forward the front of the great sacrifice drive away the waves of darkness.

sanskrit: śravo vājam iṣam ūrjaṁ vahantīr ni dāśuṣa uṣaso martyāya | maghonīr vīravat patyamānā avo dhāta vidhate ratnam adya ||
english: The dawns, bearing renown, strength, refreshment, and vigour, setting them down for the mortal worshipper — the bounteous ones, ruling with might over heroes, bestow a treasure today on the devoted singer.

sanskrit: idā hi vo vidhate ratnam astīdā vīrāya dāśuṣa uṣāsaḥ | idā viprāya jarate yad ukthā ni ṣma māvate vahathā purā cit ||
english: For here, O dawns, there is treasure for your devotee; here for the hero, for the worshipper; here for the wise man who sings when the verses are spoken — even as you have always carried to the singer in time past.

sanskrit: idā hi ta uṣo adrisāno gotrā gavām aṅgiraso gṛṇanti | vy a1rkeṇa bibhidur brahmaṇā ca satyā nṛṇām abhavad devahūtiḥ ||
english: For now, O Uṣas, Aṅgirases press the stones and sing your cow-rich enclosures; they have burst them open with hymn and with holy prayer — truly the invocation of the gods was fulfilled for those men.

sanskrit: ucchā divo duhitaḥ pratna van no bharadvājāvad vidhate maghoni | suvīraṁ rayiṁ gṛṇate rirīhy urugāyam adhi dhehi śravo naḥ ||
english: Shine forth, O daughter of heaven, as of old for us, O bounteous one, as for the devotee of Bharadvāja; flow richly to the singer with riches that bring good heroes; place upon us widely celebrated glory.

sanskrit: vapur nu tac cikituṣe cid astu samānaṁ nāma dhenu patyamānam | marteṣv anyad dohase pīpāya sakṛc chukraṁ duduhe pṛśnir ūdhaḥ ||
english: May that wonderful form be known even to the perceptive — the common name, 'the ruling cow'; among mortals another thing has swelled for the milking; the dappled one has milked her bright udder once.

sanskrit: ye agnayo na śośucann idhānā dvir yat trir maruto vāvṛdhanta | areṇavo hiraṇyayāsa eṣāṁ sākaṁ nṛmṇaiḥ pauṁsyebhiś ca bhūvan ||
english: When those who blazed like fires when kindled grew twice, thrice as the Maruts — dustless, golden, they were at once with their manly powers and strengths.

sanskrit: rudrasya ye mīḻhuṣaḥ santi putrā yāṁś co nu dādhṛvir bharadhyai | vide hi mātā maho mahī ṣā set pṛśniḥ subhve3 garbham ādhāt ||
english: Who are the sons of the bounteous Rudra — and now the steady one is to carry them; for the great mother knows their greatness — verily Pṛśni, the propitious one, has placed the germ.

sanskrit: na ya īṣante januṣo 'yā nv a1ntaḥ santo 'vadyāni punānāḥ | nir yad duhre śucayo 'nu joṣam anu śriyā tanvam ukṣamāṇāḥ ||
english: They who do not lag behind from birth, dwelling within, purifying themselves from blemishes — when the bright ones milked out according to their pleasure, sprinkling their own bodies with beauty.

sanskrit: makṣū na yeṣu dohase cid ayā ā nāma dhṛṣṇu mārutaṁ dadhānāḥ | na ye staunā ayāso mahnā nū cit sudānur ava yāsad ugrān ||
english: In whom there is quick milking too with this motion, bearing the bold name of the Maruts — who are not sluggish, nor dull in their greatness — not even now shall the good giver put down the fierce ones.

sanskrit: ta id ugrāḥ śavasā dhṛṣṇuṣeṇā ubhe yujanta rodasī sumeke | adha smaiṣu rodasī svaśocir āmavatsu tasthau na rokaḥ ||
english: Those indeed are fierce, with bold armies and strength; both heaven and earth, the well-adorned, they yoke; then among those raw-powerful ones the self-luminous heaven and earth stood like a fixed stake.

sanskrit: aneno vo maruto yāmo astv anaśvaś cid yam ajaty arathīḥ ||anavaso anabhīśū rajastūr vi rodasī pathyā yāti sādhan ||
english: May your march, O Maruts, be without fault — that which even without horse or chariot goes on; without a load, without reins, traversing the sky-dust, it goes accomplishing the road through heaven and earth.

sanskrit: nāsya vartā na tarutā nv asti maruto yam avatha vājasātau | toke vā goṣu tanaye yam apsu sa vrajaṁ dartā pārye adha dyoḥ ||
english: There is no restrainer nor overtaker of him, O Maruts, whom you protect in the winning of prizes; and him whom you protect in offspring, in cattle, in children, in the waters — he will split open the pen at the due time, at last under heaven.

sanskrit: pra citram arkaṁ gṛṇate turāya mārutāya svatavase bharadhvam | ye sahāṁsi sahasā sahante rejate agne pṛthivī makhebhyaḥ ||
english: Bring forward the bright hymn to the swift, self-strong Maruta host for the singer; those who overcome mighty powers with might — at their rites, O Agni, the earth trembles.

sanskrit: tviṣīmanto adhvarasyeva didyut tṛṣucyavaso juhvo3 nāgneḥ | arcatrayo dhunayo na vīrā bhrājajjanmāno maruto adhṛṣṭāḥ ||
english: Blazing like the lightning of the sacrifice, shaking the thirsty, like the tongue of fire — the Maruts, whose birth is brilliant, who cannot be overpowered, are three-fold radiances, like roaring heroes.

sanskrit: taṁ vṛdhantam mārutam bhrājadṛṣṭiṁ rudrasya sūnuṁ havasā vivāse | divaḥ śardhāya śucayo manīṣā girayo nāpa ugrā aspṛdhran ||
english: With my invocation I seek that growing Marutic host, of blazing brilliance, the sons of Rudra; for the host of heaven, with pure wisdom, the fierce mountains like waters have contended.

sanskrit: viśveṣāṁ vaḥ satāṁ jyeṣṭhatamā gīrbhir mitrāvaruṇā vāvṛdhadhyai | saṁ yā raśmeva yamatur yamiṣṭhā dvā janāṁ asamā bāhubhiḥ svaiḥ ||
english: O Mitra-Varuṇa, may you both, the most eminent among all the true ones, grow through these hymns; who, like a single rein, the best rulers, hold together two unequal peoples with their own arms.

sanskrit: iyam mad vām pra stṛṇīte manīṣopa priyā namasā barhir accha | yantaṁ no mitrāvaruṇāv adhṛṣṭaṁ chardir yad vāṁ varūthyaṁ sudānū ||
english: This beloved thought spreads the sacred grass forward toward you two, with a reverence; come to us, O Mitra and Varuṇa, O good givers, with your irresistible shelter, your protective covering.

sanskrit: ā yātam mitrāvaruṇā suśasty upa priyā namasā hūyamānā | saṁ yāv apnaḥstho apaseva janāñ chrudhīyataś cid yatatho mahitvā ||
english: Come hither, O Mitra and Varuṇa, by reason of this good praise, called with a dear reverence; you two who stand at activity, like activities you unite people — even those who hear you, you govern with your greatness.

sanskrit: aśvā na yā vājinā pūtabandhū ṛtā yad garbham aditir bharadhyai | pra yā mahi mahāntā jāyamānā ghorā martāya ripave ni dīdhaḥ ||
english: Those two, pure of lineage, prize-winning like horses — when Aditi by cosmic order bore the germ; those two who, being born great and mighty, have shone in dreadful fashion on the mortal who is an enemy.

sanskrit: viśve yad vām maṁhanā mandamānāḥ kṣatraṁ devāso adadhuḥ sajoṣāḥ | pari yad bhūtho rodasī cid urvī santi spaśo adabdhāso amūrāḥ ||
english: When all the gods, rejoicing in your bounty, unanimously placed dominion in you two; since you encompass even the wide heaven and earth, the spies of yours are undeceivable and unwavering.

sanskrit: tā hi kṣatraṁ dhārayethe anu dyūn dṛṁhethe sānum upamād iva dyoḥ | dṛḻho nakṣatra uta viśvadevo bhūmim ātān dyāṁ dhāsināyoḥ ||
english: For you two sustain dominion day after day; you two strengthen the summit like the height of heaven; the firm star and the all-divine — of those two who adorn the earth and sky, it has been established.

sanskrit: tā vigraṁ dhaithe jaṭharam pṛṇadhyā ā yat sadma sabhṛtayaḥ pṛṇanti | na mṛṣyante yuvatayo 'vātā vi yat payo viśvajinvā bharante ||
english: You two fill the capacious womb — when those who are well-laden fill the abode; the young women untouched by wind are not diminished when the all-nourishing ones spread forth the milk.

sanskrit: tā jihvayā sadam edaṁ sumedhā ā yad vāṁ satyo aratir ṛte bhūt | tad vām mahitvaṁ ghṛtānnāv astu yuvaṁ dāśuṣe vi cayiṣṭam aṁhaḥ ||
english: With the tongue, O wise ones, always this praise — when your true hymn of praise is found in the rite; let your greatness be that, O you who eat the oblation of ghee; may you two remove the distress from the worshipper.

sanskrit: pra yad vām mitrāvaruṇā spūrdhan priyā dhāma yuvadhitā minanti | na ye devāsa ohasā na martā ayajñasāco apyo na putrāḥ ||
english: When the rivals of you two, O Mitra-Varuṇa, make away with your favourite abode established for you both — neither do the gods do this by challenge, nor mortals, those without sacrifice, the watery ones — not even their sons.

sanskrit: vi yad vācaṁ kīstāso bharante śaṁsanti ke cin nivido manānāḥ | ād vām bravāma satyāny ukthā nakir devebhir yatatho mahitvā ||
english: When the praisers spread abroad the voice, and some, thinking them the nivids, proclaim — then we speak true praises to you; with your greatness no one contends even among the gods.

sanskrit: avor itthā vāṁ chardiṣo abhiṣṭau yuvor mitrāvaruṇāv askṛdhoyu | anu yad gāvaḥ sphurān ṛjipyaṁ dhṛṣṇuṁ yad raṇe vṛṣaṇaṁ yunajan ||
english: Verily in this way, O Mitra and Varuṇa, your shelter in attack has been made without decay; when the cows kicked back the swift, bold bull and yoked the virile one for battle.
